To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
food processing can enhance phenolic compounds release from the matrix (bioaccessibility) and their absorption and transfer into the bloodstream (bioavailability).

(i) food processing can increase phenolic compounds bioavailability and bioaccessibility; (ii) the effects of processing are dependent of phenolic compounds and food matrices; (iii) processing strategies can be used to increase phenolic compounds solubility; (iv) processing strategies can increase the release from the food matrix; (v) processing strategies can enhance the absorption of phenolic compounds; and (vi) processing strategies can improve phenolic compounds stability.

the bioaccessibility and/or bioavailability of phenolic compounds in foods can be enhanced by processing, and that the effects of processing depend on the chemical structure of phenolic compounds and on the food matrix.
In summary, our research is concerned with
food processing as a strategy for enhancing phenolic compounds bioavailability in plant based-foods.
the development of food processing technologies to enhance phenolic bioavailability and bioaccessibility.
the effects of food processing on the bioaccessibility and the bioavailability of phenolic compounds in foods.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
processing can be used to enhance bioaccessibility or/and bioavailability, however, it depends on the food matrix and on the specific processing conditions applied.
food processing is not detrimental for the bioavailability of phenolic compounds and that, in most of cases, it is beneficial.
food processing can enhance phenolic compounds’ bioaccessibility and/or bioavailability, but this is not a general rule.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

food processing can be a powerful strategy to enhance phenolic compound bioaccessibility and/or bioavailability, however, the effects of processing should be assessed in the context of the food matrix.

processing strategies can be used to enhance phenolic compound bioaccessibility and/or bioavailability in plant foods, and that these strategies can be applied to the design of healthier plant-based foods.
food processing can be a useful tool to enhance the bioaccessibility and/or bioavailability of phenolic compounds.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of processing should be evaluated on bioaccessibility and not on the total content, as it is the only way to predict the biological activity of phenolics.
food processing is a key factor in the bioaccessibility and the bioavailability of phenolic compounds.
food processing can be used as a strategy to improve the bioaccessibility and the bioavailability of phenolic compounds in foods.
